newsitem.title: USA: NASA considers early shuttle launch.
newsitem.headline: NASA considers early shuttle launch.

text.p: NASA managers were considering moving up Tuesday's planned launch of the space shuttle Columbia to dodge afternoon thunderstorms, an official for the U.S. space agency said on Monday.
The shuttle's launch time on Tuesday could be moved 47 minutes earlier to 1:50 p.m. EDT (1750 GMT), NASA spokesman Bruce Buckingham said.
"This is a really good possibility," he said. "We want to try to get our launch off before the storms roll through."

U.S. Air Force meteorologists offered a grim forecast for the shuttle's planned 2:37 p.m. EDT (1837 GMT) blastoff from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre. They gave the shuttle only a 10 percent chance of fair weather for launch.
Thunderstorms and rain showers were expected to form along the east coast of Florida and there was also potential for severe weather that could damage an exposed shuttle on the launch pad.
"If we can get off the ground it's going to be early (afternoon)," shuttle weather officer Ed Priselac told a news conference earlier on Monday.
Mission managers were to meet again on Monday afternoon to decide whether to launch earlier than planned.
Meanwhile engineers reported no technical problems with Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four space shuttles.
The winged spaceship is to make a second attempt at a 16-day research mission that was cut short in April after just five days because of a troublesome power generator.
